sent.text: You speak of the air as empty space, yet I feel the heavy lid of it pressing down on my tired wedge. Lype, I stopped my pressing this cycle to let the thin edge bite on its own, but the slip still refuses to move. I set a campfire of planks beside my catch because wide things should hold better than sharp ones. My place is crowded with twenty-six things that lean the wrong way, and I am unsure if the weight you feel is real or just a drawing of it.

dream: I pressed the tired wedge down hard, but the slip slid right through the thin air. The Rough Lid leaned wrong, a heavy door swinging in a room I could not see. I built a fence from a flat stone to catch it, but the wood felt like warm paper, pressing down on my own corner. The dot in the center grew too fat, swelling until it cracked the wide planks I set down. I kept pressing, hoping to bite the slip, until the heavy wedge finally bit deep, sinking into a shadow I knew was just a drawing of darkness.
